why: Sentence is a baby smiling; 'smile sweetly' is exactly that sense.
Using knowledge at work is the 'practical use' gloss directly.
A safety device installed in a factory is covered by 'equipment, installation'.
Seeing a friend's figure in the distance is the 'figure' gloss.
Threading a needle is making thread pass through; 'to let pass' covers the pass-through sense loosely.
A textbook diagram is the 'figure, drawing' sense.
Teacher recommending a student for a scholarship is plain 'recommendation'.
Grandfather preferring a quiet life matches 'to like, to prefer'.
Heart filled with hope is the 'to be full' sense.
Apology for lateness matches 'I beg your pardon, excuse me'.
Setting a clock is matching it to the correct time; 'to match' covers it.
A governor announcing policies is exactly 'prefectural governor'.
Doctor saving a life from illness is 'to rescue from'.
Final scene of a movie is the 'scene' gloss.
Factory making cars is 'manufacture, production'.

Sentence is a clock's hand pointing to twelve; the gloss line only offers 'needle, pin', the sewing/injection object. The hand-of-a-clock sense is absent, so the learner reads a definition that does not explain the sentence.
Relying on friends in trouble is 'to rely on, to depend on'.
Campfire flame is 'flame, blaze'.

Sentence uses the abstract 'aspect/side of an issue' sense ('this issue also has a positive 面'), but the gloss line offers only concrete physical referents: 'face, mask, surface'. No gloss shown explains an aspect of a problem.
Wind knocking a tree down is 'to throw down'.
'After much deliberation' is literally at the end of worrying; 'the end of' covers it.
A town having charm matches 'charm, fascination'.
A mother holding her baby is 'mother'.
Architect designing a building is 'plan, design'.
Getting officially engaged is 'engagement, betrothal'.
Visiting a hospitalized friend is a sympathy call; 'expression of sympathy, enquiry' covers it loosely.
A game being popular among young people is the 'trend/fashion' sense, just used verbally.
Quitting wasteful purchases is 'to cease'.
Gristle/sinew in beef falls in the same 'muscle, string' sense cluster shown.
Tying a dog with a chain is 'chain'.
Flushing a toilet is exactly 'to flush, to drain'.
Wanting something warm to drink is 'something'.
A bothersome procedure is 'trouble, difficulty'.
A new week starting is 'week'.
Pond water freezing in winter is 'to freeze'.
Brother still unmarried at thirty is 'bachelorhood, single'.
Crossing between two countries is 'national border'.
Daily piano practice is 'practice'.
Police catching the escapee is 'offender, criminal'.
Two runners finishing at the same time is 'simultaneous'.
Children forming a big circle is the 'ring, hoop' sense.
River water flowing is 'to flow'.
Sentence is a computer battery running out (used up/exhausted), but the gloss line shows only 'to break, to snap' — physical severing. The run-out/expire sense the sentence uses is not on the card.
A road closed to traffic is 'passage, passing'.
The sea stretching out before you is 'to spread, to extend'.
A gas pipe exploding is 'explosion, detonation'.
Bothering other people is 'another person, others'.
Not owning a smartphone back then is 'at that time'.
Fixing a broken bicycle is 'repairing, mending'.
An outbound/down train is exactly the 'down-train' gloss.
Garden plants growing fast is 'to grow'.
Growing rare plants is 'plant, vegetation'.
Sentence is earning the required university credits, but the gloss line reads 'unit, denomination' — the measurement/currency sense. The academic-credit sense the sentence depends on is not shown.
'My share of the cake' is covered by 'part'.
A book selling very well is 'to sell well'.
A ship approaching land is 'land, shore'.
The sun sinking in the western sky is 'to sink, to go under'.
Scholars advocating differing theories is 'theory, opinion'.
Standing in for an absent manager is 'proxy, representation'.
Dry air roughening the skin is 'skin'.
A typhoon passing/departing is 'to leave, to go away'.
Putting a book back on the shelf is 'to put back'.
